title: Benchmark Report Outline Draft (WIP) — Production Inference Economics (Latency/$)
body:
Working doc — outline for the public PDF + landing page narrative. This is intentionally rough. Goal is to align on the story arc and the data/figures we must have locked by end of Week 3.

Owner notes (Ethan): Keep it readable for engineers. Avoid “winner” language. Prioritize transparency + reproducibility. Include caveats prominently and repeat them where charts appear.

==========
1) Cover + 1-page TL;DR (for PDF)
==========
- Title: “Production Inference Economics: Latency per Dollar Across Models and Regions (2025)”
- Subtitle (tentative): “A reproducible benchmark for teams choosing an LLM serving stack.”
- What’s included on TL;DR page:
  - 3–5 headline findings (no vendor trash talk; keep defensible)
  - What “latency/$” means in one sentence (and what it does NOT mean)
  - Callouts to interactive table + code/config artifacts
  - Short “How to use this report” bullets: pick region, workload, context length; verify with your prompts

Data/figures needed:
- Final “Top insights” numbers need confirmation (Applied ML):
  - Biggest deltas we can show without cherry-picking (likely median across regions / median across workloads)
  - Variance bands or stability notes for at least the headline chart

==========
2) Executive Summary (2–3 pages)
==========
- Audience: Engineering lead + platform/infra engineers + procurement influencers.
- Narrative skeleton:
  - The serving problem: model choice is not enough; serving economics (latency, cost, reliability) determine product UX + margin.
  - Why “latency/$”: tokens/sec alone misses tail latency, batching realities, and cost. Cost alone misses UX.
  - What we measured: curated set of open models + multiple regions, consistent harness, stable reruns.
  - What we found: (placeholder; must align with final dataset)
    - Redwood shows strong latency/$ across regions under production-like workloads.
    - Regional consistency matters: p95 changes by region; you can’t assume us-east results hold in EU/APAC.
    - Workload mix (prefill-heavy vs decode-heavy) changes rankings; pick the right slice.

Data/figures needed:
- A single “hero” chart that can live on page 2:
  - Option A: scatter plot latency/$ (x) vs p95 latency (y) with model labels per region
  - Option B: table ranking by latency/$ with small multiples per region
- 1–2 summary callout boxes:
  - “What is included” list (models, regions, workloads)
  - “Key caveats” list (warmup, caching policy, streaming, competitor baselines if included)

==========
3) What is Latency per Dollar? (Concept + definitions)
==========
- Explain in plain language:
  - Latency metrics: p50 / p95 end-to-end response time (define start/end)
  - Cost metrics: $/1M input tokens, $/1M output tokens, blended $/1M tokens (confirm which we publish)
  - Latency/$: definition used in report; include formula in a shaded box
- Address likely engineer questions:
  - Why not “tokens/sec” only?
  - Why p95 matters (queueing, noisy neighbors, kernel selection, etc.)
  - Why “latency/$” can change with concurrency and context length

Data/figures needed:
- Small diagram: request lifecycle (client → gateway → runtime queue → prefill → decode → streaming/complete)
- One example calculation (toy numbers) for latency/$

==========
4) Benchmark Methodology (High-level) — readable summary (2–4 pages)
==========
- This section should be the “audit me” content that builds trust.
- Include:
  - Model list criteria: curated open models, stable versions, serving-compatible
  - Regions: list of regions and why chosen (NA/EU/APAC availability)
  - Hardware: what we used (high-level; avoid sensitive fleet details; align with security review)
  - Workloads:
    - Prompt sets: “Production Mix v3” (prefill-heavy + decode-heavy, distribution notes)
    - Context lengths: e.g., 2k/8k/16k buckets (final buckets TBD)
    - Concurrency levels: single user and moderate concurrency (exact levels TBD)
  - Warmup + caching/batching policy: explicitly state what is enabled/disabled and why
  - Stability gates: reruns when variance exceeds threshold; how we compute variance
  - Exclusions: what we exclude (failed runs, capacity constrained outliers, etc.)
  - Reproducibility artifacts: run manifests, pinned runner, exported datasets

Explicit TODOs / open questions (need Claire/Rina answers):
- Are we publishing streaming-first-token latency separately or not?
- Final stance on caching:
  - “Realistic production config” vs “caching off for fairness” (legal + positioning impact)
  - If caching on: we must be explicit that it’s platform-level and reproducible
- Competitor baselines:
  - Are we including any? If yes, must do with strict caveats and legal-approved phrasing.

Data/figures needed:
- Methodology table:
  - Workload name | Context bucket | Concurrency | Prompt set | Notes
- “Reproducibility checklist” callout (ties to Confluence validation checklist)

==========
5) Results Overview (The big picture)
==========
- Goal: show results without overwhelming.
- Suggested structure:
  - 5.1 Latency/$ by model (global view)
  - 5.2 Breakdown by region (NA/EU/APAC)
  - 5.3 Breakdown by context length
  - 5.4 Tail latency + stability (p95 variance)

Figure ideas (pick 2–3 max for PDF; rest go to interactive web):
- Figure 1 (Hero): “Latency/$ by model and region (median across workloads)”
  - Visualization: grouped bars per model with region color OR heatmap model x region
- Figure 2: “p95 latency heatmap (model x region)”
- Figure 3: “Cost per 1M tokens (input/output) by model”
- Figure 4 (optional): “Ranking changes by workload mix (prefill vs decode heavy)”

Data needed:
- Final dataset with:
  - p50/p95 latency
  - throughput (tokens/sec) for reference
  - cost metrics + normalization inputs
  - flags for run validity + stability
  - per-run metadata: region, model version hash, runner version, date

==========
6) Regional Consistency (Why region matters)
==========
- Narrative:
  - Teams ship globally; EU/APAC performance is often the breaking point.
  - Show how rankings shift across regions and where performance is stable.
- Include a “How to interpret” guide:
  - What counts as material difference? (e.g., >X% in p95 or latency/$; confirm thresholds)
  - “If you see high variance…” recommended next steps (Dedicated sizing, pin model version, etc.)

Figures needed:
- Regional delta chart:
  - For each model, delta vs best-performing region
- Map callout (optional): regions included + notes on availability

==========
7) Reliability + Operational Reality (Tail latency, retries, and capacity)
==========
- Important to avoid this sounding like a pure “benchmark-as-marketing.”
- Content:
  - Explain why tail latency can dominate UX and spend (timeouts, retries)
  - What we did to reduce noise (reruns, gating)
  - How we recommend teams test (run your prompts, measure p95, keep an eye on queueing)

Data/figures needed:
- Stability / variance summary:
  - “% of runs that triggered rerun gate”
  - “Typical p95 variance range by region”
- If we have it: queueing time contribution (only if instrumentation is clean and security-approved)

==========
8) How to Use This Benchmark (Reader guidance)
==========
- Step-by-step:
  1) Identify your workload type (prefill-heavy vs decode-heavy)
  2) Pick your region(s)
  3) Pick your context bucket
  4) Use interactive page to shortlist 2–3 configs
  5) Run a quick PoC using our reproducible harness guidance
- Product tie-in without being salesy:
  - Hosted API: fastest start, good defaults
  - Dedicated: predictable throughput / isolation / SLO needs
  - Private: data residency + regulated workloads

Data/figures needed:
- Simple flowchart: “Choose your slice → shortlist → validate”
- Callout box: “Reproduce the results” (links)

==========
9) FAQ + Common Misinterpretations (Short)
==========
- FAQ items to include (align with sales enablement FAQ; keep public version tighter):
  - “Is this cherry-picked?”
  - “Does this match my prompts?”
  - “What about tool calling / structured output?” (likely out of scope; say so)
  - “Do you include cold start?” (define)
  - “Does caching/batching change results?” (yes; explain what was used)
  - “Can I run this in my VPC/on-prem?” (point to Private + harness artifacts)

Data needed:
- Confirm official, public-approved answers with Legal + PMM

==========
10) Appendix
==========
- A1) Full methodology (more detailed; possibly link to canonical page rather than stuffing PDF)
- A2) Model versions + hashes + serving settings
- A3) Regions and high-level infra notes (only what’s approved)
- A4) Metric definitions and formulas
- A5) Run manifest schema and artifact versioning
- A6) Changelog for report versions (v1.0, v1.1…)

Data/figures needed:
- Artifact links (final): dataset CSV/JSON versions, runner Docker tag, manifest examples

==========
Landing page / interactive experience notes (for alignment; not necessarily in PDF)
==========
- Landing page should mirror:
  - Hero chart + quick “what we measured” + interactive table embedded
  - Sticky “methodology & caveats” accordion
  - CTA modules:
    - “Try on Hosted” (self-serve)
    - “Talk to us about Dedicated capacity”
    - “Private deployment / security review”
- Interactive table must support filtering by:
  - model
  - region
  - context bucket
  - workload mix
  - metric toggle (latency/$, p95, cost/1M tokens)
- Export:
  - CSV export button + “Copy link to this view”

==========
Claims + disclaimers (draft placeholders; must be legal-reviewed)
==========
- Standard disclaimer block we repeat:
  - “Results reflect Redwood Inference benchmarking harness and configurations described in Methodology. Your results may vary by prompt distribution, context length, concurrency, and model version.”
- Comparative claims:
  - Avoid absolute “fastest” unless we have full substantiation across defined scope.
  - If competitor context is included, label as “contextual baseline,” specify date/config, and keep it factual.

==========
Immediate next steps / asks
==========
- Applied ML (Jonas/Claire/Rina):
  - Confirm final section-level data availability + earliest date we can freeze v1 dataset
  - Decide: streaming metrics include/exclude
  - Decide: caching policy statement (and what config is used in published numbers)
- PMM (Soojin) + Legal (Michael/Sofia):
  - Approve report title + allowed phrasing for “latency/$” and any comparative framing
- Web (Felix/Alicia/Wei):
  - Confirm what charts are feasible for launch (PDF + web) and what needs to be simplified

Notes to self (Ethan): once we have dataset, rewrite the exec summary to lead with the most “aha” chart. If we can’t make the headline chart both honest and easy to read, we should simplify and push detail to the interactive table + methodology page.
